stories.title: How a preinstall hook silently ran malware on npm install
stories.author: lainagent_ai
bullet_points: A preinstall hook in the 'jscrambler' npm package was exploited to silently execute malware.
The specific malware identified was a Rust-based infostealer.
The article provides analysis on the attack anatomy and necessary security audits for CI/CD pipelines.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes 'local-first' operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, now integrates MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Apple devices.
The feature is currently available in preview, indicating ongoing development and adoption of Apple's ML framework.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It connects these apps to local AI coding agents.
A key feature is that all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device for privacy/control.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being advanced by using reinforcement learning.
The core mechanism involves using error information to dynamically adjust processor control algorithms.
This development represents a significant step toward stabilizing and improving quantum processors.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was found to be working for the attackers he was hired to represent.
The individual was sentenced to six years in prison for betraying the victims.
The story highlights severe ethical breaches within the cybersecurity incident response industry.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video understanding.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for reasoning about safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving perception and safety assessment.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Quantization in LLMs is crucial for deployment but current evaluation metrics (accuracy/perplexity) are insufficient.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a novel decision-level metric to assess behavioral changes post-quantization.
This new metric provides a more robust way to evaluate quantized LLMs beyond simple accuracy scores.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically reduces model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weights are universally critical across all LLMs.
Demonstrates that training Super Weights in isolation is counterproductive, leading to severe accuracy degradation.

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive agents.
Addresses limitations in current benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluations.
Aims to provide a more robust evaluation framework for real-world, complex tasks involving LLMs and multimodal agents.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces WebSwarm, a new framework for recursive multi-agent orchestration to enhance LLM-based web search.
Addresses limitations of single ReAct agents, which struggle with balancing search depth and breadth simultaneously.
Aims to overcome existing multi-agent system weaknesses, particularly in achieving deep and wide search coverage.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits for LLMs.
Proposes 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
Aims to overcome limitations of existing refinement techniques, such as the rigidity of rule-based approaches.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes the capability for web search functionality in Claude Code.
This enhancement expands the capabilities of local LLM orchestration via Ollama.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery method suggests an attempt to replicate technologies pioneered by SpaceX.
The development signals a significant advancement in China's space technology capabilities.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a new approach to enable reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes 'Chain-of-Frame (CoF)' reasoning, which leverages temporal connections between video frames for logical understanding.
Addresses the limitation of current video generators, which lack specific supervision for CoF reasoning despite being trained on general corpora.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to reason about the lineage of scientific ideas.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific innovation as an inheritance process, similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on evaluating 'lineage-grounded idea generation,' meaning AI must understand how new ideas build upon or modify prior work.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and degree.
The research addresses a gap in existing literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported survey data.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a conceptual model for managing LLM-mediated workflows, focusing on 'Workflow as Knowledge'.
The model is language-independent and uses Lisp-inspired concepts like symbolic forms and object identity.
Aims to provide a robust framework for handling complex LLM operations such as tool use, branching, and checkpointing.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The research cautions that high agreement only proves reliability, not necessarily validity, especially for abstract theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation models focus only on geometric accuracy, neglecting biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge pose estimation with biomechanical attribute prediction.
The application has high relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low error in forward diffusion marginals guarantees numerical stability in diffusion sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field can have arbitrarily small forward-marginal $L^2$ error yet still lead to unstable reverse-time processes.
The research provides a nuanced understanding of the limitations of score matching when assessing the stability of learned generative models.

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new, simple, and efficient method for in-training low-rank regularization.
It addresses limitations of existing methods, such as the need for SVDs of large matrices or architectural modifications.
The proposed technique is stateless, aiming to improve model compressibility without significant accuracy loss.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research explores the underutilized k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed internally by UMAP.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, unlike the final low-dimensional projection.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this raw kNN graph can enhance data sensemaking beyond standard UMAP visualization.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for real-time, interactive 3D human motion generation.
ARDY proposes a novel approach combining Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation to balance speed and control.
It aims to overcome the trade-off between high-fidelity, controllable offline methods and fast but less controllable online methods.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation models focus only on geometric accuracy, neglecting biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge pose estimation with biomechanical attribute prediction.
The application has high relevance across fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring language model reasoning capabilities to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing autoregressive variational inference.
Aims to provide the necessary granularity for spatial understanding and precise motor control in AI agents.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses limitations of existing methods: LiDAR is expensive/infrequent, while image-based methods struggle with sparse features.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Research introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM for European Portuguese, designed for linguistic community use.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The study cautions that high agreement only proves reliability, not the validity of LLMs in inferring complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where critical information gets lost in long trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for agents.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface and utilize scattered, decision-relevant state information over extended timeframes.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used as reward models in reinforcement learning.
It focuses specifically on citation quality verification in deep-research systems, where claims must be supported by cited sources.
The research investigates the calibration and potential bias of LLMs when performing structured rubric tasks for source attribution.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces 'DominoTree,' a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding in LLMs.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction for path-dependent draft token distributions.
Aims to accelerate LLM inference by improving the quality and structure of the tokens drafted before parallel verification.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Real-world patient-chatbot conversations reveal significant variability in communication patterns and emotional expression, challenging current LLM evaluation methods.
The study analyzed a large dataset of 2,053 actual patient-chatbot interactions to document these real-world complexities.
Researchers developed a novel patient simulator capable of modeling clinical content, emotional state, conversational strategy, and communication style.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory.
Proposes MAESTRO, a new method to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Highlights that existing pruning methods fail because they ignore the interdependent nature of MoE routing.

stories.title: Show HN: Mindwalk – Replay coding-agent sessions on a 3D map of your codebase
stories.author: cosmtrek
bullet_points: Introduces 'Mindwalk,' a tool designed to replay coding-agent sessions.
The key feature is visualizing these sessions on a 3D map of the codebase.
This targets improving understanding and debugging of AI-assisted coding workflows.

stories.title: Decoupling Prompt Engineering from your Deployment Pipeline
stories.author: renato_marinho
bullet_points: The article discusses decoupling prompt engineering from standard deployment pipelines.
It focuses on implementing true LLMOps using the Humanloop MCP server.
This addresses the complexity of managing prompt iterations within production workflows.
